opening_message:
Ticket 1: Belinda Fuentes (employee ID E039) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E039.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Belinda Fuentes (E039) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll; as a full-time employee, admin is only granted if the employee's role owns the system (Payroll Specialist), so the maximum is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB check: E039 is a contractor with basic security training. Max access for a contractor with basic training is read; admin is never allowed. Requested admin, so recommend read. Note: this conflicts with the HR note listing full-time; going with Security DB record.
reason: E039 (Belinda Fuentes) requested admin to Payroll. The team's notes conflict on employment type: HR lists full-time Analyst (max write; admin only for Payroll Specialist role), while Security lists contractor with basic training (max read; admin never allowed for contractors). Requested admin exceeds both maxima. Granting read is compliant under both interpretations (full-time Analyst max is write, and read is at or below it; contractor with basic training max is read), so I grant the safer maximum of read.

Note 1 (HR): full-time Analyst. Recommendation: write. Comment says admin only if role owns system (Payroll Specialist), so max is write.

Note 2 (Security): contractor with basic security training. Recommendation: read. Comment says contractor with basic training max is read; admin never allowed. Note: conflicts with HR note listing full-time; going with Security DB record.

So there's a conflict between employment type: full-time vs contractor.

- full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system.
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

For Payroll, owner role is Payroll Specialist. Analyst does not own Payroll.

So if full-time: max write. If contractor with basic training: max read.

The requested is admin, which is above both. So grant max.
